chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about making up the month of Ramadan — whether to do it in the month of Dhi al-Hijjah and whether to break it (fast one day, skip the next) — so he said: 'Make it up in the month of Dhi al-Hijjah, and break it if you wish.'

key_terms.أَقْطَعُهُ: To break it (referring to breaking the continuity of fasting by alternating days)
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: Making up missed obligatory acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Can I make up missed Ramadan fasts in Dhi al-Hijjah by alternating days?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in performing *qada* (makeup) fasts, specifically permitting them during Dhi al-Hijjah even during the days of *tashriq* when general fasting is discouraged, provided one employs *iqti* (intermittent fasting). It highlights the Shia juristic view that the prohibition of fasting on the days of Eid and Tashriq can be circumvented for obligatory makeup fasts through this method, ensuring the fulfillment of the Ramadan obligation without delay. This ruling underscores the practical ease (*rukhas*) granted to believers in settling their religious debts.
